description.narrative: World Space Week has been officially declared by the United Nations as the annual week from 4 to 10 October. It is an international celebration of the contribution of space science and technology to improving the human condition. The dates that mark World Space Week commemorate landmark events of the space age: on 4 October 1957, Sputnik I, the first man-made Earth satellite, was launched. The Treaty on the Peaceful Exploration of Outer Space was signed by UN member states on 10 October 1967. The celebration of World Space Week is an excellent opportunity to highlight the achievements and potential of space exploration on a global level. World Space Week usually takes place in October and involves a variety of activities, including talks, workshops, exhibitions, competitions and much more. On 4 October 1957, the launch into outer space of the first man-made Earth satellite, Sputnik 1, paved the way for space exploration. A decade later, on 10 October 1967, the Treaty on the Principles Governing the Activities of States in the Exploration and Use of Outer Space, including the Moon and Other Celestial Bodies entered into force. Space science and technology and their applications are increasingly being used to support a wide range of United Nations activities. At least 25 United Nations entities and the World Bank Group routinely use space applications. They make important and sometimes essential contributions to the work of the United Nations, including in implementing the recommendations of major world conferences and the Third United Nations Conference on the Exploration and Peaceful Uses of Outer Space (UNISPACE III), as well as in supporting sustainable development. Since the dawn of the Space Age, the United Nations has recognised that outer space has added a new dimension to humanity's existence. The United Nations family continually strives to utilise the unique benefits of outer space for the betterment of all humanity. Recognising humanity's common interest in outer space and seeking to answer questions about how outer space can help benefit the peoples of the Earth, the General Assembly adopted its first resolution related to outer space, resolution 1348 (XIII) entitled "Question of the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space".
